column1: # Every backend service that has, or will have, its own pod.
# Status displays read this rather than the directory listing, so a service that
# has not been written yet shows as "not built yet" instead of quietly not
# appearing. During a build, what is missing is the more useful half of the
# Columns are tab separated: name, domain, phase, purpose.
#   phase  built      running now, as its own deployment
#          later      in the architecture, not in this pass
#          external   not written here; deployed and merged from upstream
# One row is one deployment. That is deliberately NOT the same list as
# system-architecture.html §3, which names capabilities rather than pods: the
# entitlement record and the module registry are tables inside Tenant, and the
# onboarding checklist is literally the provisioning saga's own rows. None of
# the three has a lifecycle of its own, so none of them is a pod, and a row here
# for something that can never be started or stopped would be a line of noise in
# a display whose whole job is what is up and what is down. Where each one lives
# is written into its host's purpose below.
# So: do not re-add a row because §3 lists it. Add a row when something earns a
# deployment. Build order and reasoning: backend-plan.md. Order is the order

column4: purpose
Terminates /api, verifies tokens, resolves the tenant, checks permissions
Terminates /admin/api on its own host: staff session, MFA, IP allowlist. Never shares an auth path with /api
Identity: credentials, sessions, PASETO tokens, merchant codes
Authorisation: roles, permission sets, plane isolation
Drains every service's outbox onto Kafka. The only Kafka producer
Phase 0 canary. Proves ingress, registry and rollout still work
Items, services, prices, tax rules, modifiers. One source of truth
Staff records, roles, rotas, availability, and the tier's seat quota
Stock levels, reservations, adjustments, low-stock thresholds
Authorise, capture, refund. Swapped per market
Registering a sale: cart, tender, tabs, voids, refunds, takings, the floor
Customer documents AND the tenant's own subscription billing. Swapped per market
Calendar, slots, deposits, no-shows, buffers, double-booking prevention
Dashboard queries over ClickHouse. Never queries operational stores
Business identity, trade, hours, tax, locale. Also the entitlement record and the module registry: one record, written and read in one transaction
Runs the provisioning saga: per-step state, retries, compensation. Its rows are the merchant's 24-hour checklist
Templates, branding, channel preference, quiet hours, delivery log
Only writer to object storage; signed URL issue
Plain-language record of every automated decision
Cron, reminders, the six-hour budget cycle, nightly reconciliation
Impersonation: time limited, read-only by default, and recorded. The merchant is not asked first
Double-entry journal for this environment's single legal entity
Site templates, pages, publishing, custom domain requests
Order lines to prep stations, claimed and passed. A trade capability inside POS, not a sold module
Bidirectional pipeline to Twenty, and the ID mapping
Budget allocation against booked revenue, every six hours
Campaign, spend and conversion sync with the ad platforms
Ad copy and imagery generation, creative variant testing
The forked Twenty CRM. Its own deployment and its own PostgreSQL
